# Old Persian: the carved sign sequence (generated by tools/build_op_signs.ts; D-176, D-177)

What is carved: the published sign-by-sign transliteration in Kent's convention (Kent 1953 / Lecoq 1997), data/corpus/op_translit.json
(D-176), word by word and line by line; slips of the copy are corrected only as listed in data/corpus/op_sign_decisions.json, each with its
evidence. Schmitt's edition (ARIo, CC0; the text the translation layer shows) is compared word by word: Kent's spelling rules on his
word give the carved signs (`same`), or differ only by a written glide (`glide`), or the stone writes a logogram (`logogram`), or the two
editions read differently (`reading`: Q-288); `corpus-only` words are carved, `ario-only` words are not. DPh (sealed plates) has no
corpus copy and is not carved.

Columns: corpus = corpus words carved; same/glide/logogram/reading = aligned word groups; corrected = corpus words corrected (listed);
lost = signs lost in the corpus, left uncut; ario = Schmitt's words.

## Corrections of the copy (data/corpus/op_sign_decisions.json)

| Text | copy | read | × | evidence | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| XPa | Xšhayâršâm | Xšayâršâm | 1 | ario | a stray h: the king's name has no ha sign (xa-ša-ya-a-ra-ša-a-ma, Schmitt's Xšayaṛšām); the copy spells the name without it everywhere else |
| XPa | Hâxâmaniš|iya | Haxâmaniš|iya | 1 | ario | a stray length mark: Haxāmanišiya (ha-xa-a-…), Schmitt's reading and the copy's spelling in every other text |
| XPb | xsh|âiyathiyahyâ | xsh|âyathiyahyâ | 1 | ario | a stray i before y: xa-ša-a-ya-θa-i-ya-ha-ya-a as Schmitt's xšāyaθiyahyā and as the copy spells the word in the other XP texts |
| XPc | upâ | utâ | 1 | ario | p for t: the conjunction utā (u-ta-a), Schmitt's reading, and the copy's spelling everywhere else |
| DNa | bumâm | bûmim | 1 | ario | the accusative būmim (ba-u-mi-i-ma), Schmitt's reading and the copy's own spelling in DNa line 1-2 and the XP texts |
| DNa | tvašâm | tyašâm | 1 | ario | v for y: tya-šām (ta-ya-ša-a-ma), Schmitt's tayašām |
| DNa | adâraiya | adâraya | 1 | ario | a stray i: adāraya (a-da-a-ra-ya), Schmitt's reading and the copy's own spelling of the verb in DNa |
| DNa | g|âthun | g|âthum | 1 | ario | n for m: the accusative gāθum (ga-a-θa-u-ma), Schmitt's reading |
| DNb | v|inâithayatiy | v|inâthayatiy | 1 | ario | a stray i: vināθayatiy (vi-i-na-a-θa-ya-ta-i-ya), Schmitt's vināθayati |
| DNb | vinâthayais | vinâthayaiš | 1 | ario | s for š: vināθayaiš, Schmitt's vināθayai̯š and the copy's own spelling two words later |
| DNb | uta | utâ | 1 | ario | a lost length mark: utā (u-ta-a), Schmitt's reading and the copy's spelling everywhere else |
| DNb | xšnnutam | xšnutam | 1 | convention | a doubled n, which Kent's convention never writes (the script writes no gemination): xšnutam |
| DPc | Dârayavauš | Dârayavahauš | 1 | ario | the genitive the phrase needs ('in the house of king Darius'): Dārayavahauš (da-a-ra-ya-va-ha-u-ša), Schmitt's reading; the nominative is a slip of the copy |
| DPc | xšhyâ | XŠhyâ | 1 | copy | the logogram XŠ with its complement -hyā, as the copy writes the same word in XPc and XPi (XŠhyâ); lower case xšhyâ would spell xa-ša-ha-ya-a, no Old Persian word |
| DPd | Aura|mazda | Aura|mazdâ | 1 | ario | a lost length mark: Auramazdā (…-za-da-a), Schmitt's reading and the copy's spelling everywhere else |
| DPe | xšâyathya | xšâyathiya | 1 | ario | a lost i: xšāyaθiya (xa-ša-a-ya-θa-i-ya), Schmitt's reading and the copy's spelling 39 times elsewhere |
| DPe | Darayavauš | Dârayavauš | 1 | ario | a lost length mark: Dārayavauš (da-a-ra-…), Schmitt's reading and the copy's spelling everywhere else |
